findings.title: Device-limit rejection is bypassable by retrying with the same device ID
findings.body: In tagDeviceUI the local cache entry is set before CreateOrUpdateDevice. When CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry remains. TagDevice propagates the error so the first anonymous authentication request fails, but any subsequent request with the same X-Grafana-Device-Id on the same instance within the 29-minute local-cache TTL sees the cached key and returns nil without touching the store. Anonymous.Authenticate then succeeds, so a client can bypass the configured device limit simply by retrying.

findings.title: Clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the device ID header
findings.body: TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is empty. Since Anonymous.Authenticate now only rejects when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, an anonymous request that omits this header is never counted and always proceeds even when the configured limit has been reached. If the device limit is intended to be enforced, missing or empty device IDs should not silently skip enforcement.

findings.title: Device limit check and insert are not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first calls CountDevices and then, if count < deviceLimit, performs an upsert. There is no transaction, lock, or database-enforced cap around these two operations. Concurrent requests from different devices can all observe a count below the limit and then insert, so the configured device limit can be exceeded under normal concurrent anonymous traffic.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now blocks on synchronous device-store writes
findings.body: Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously before returning an identity. On a local-cache miss, TagDevice performs a database count when the limit is enabled and an insert/update upsert for each new device, and again after the 29-minute local-cache TTL. Previously this work ran in a background goroutine with a timeout and did not delay login. This adds database latency and database-availability risk to the anonymous authentication path.

findings.title: RowsAffected == 0 can incorrectly reject existing devices on MySQL
findings.body: updateDevice treats RowsAffected() == 0 as proof that no existing device was updated and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL default behavior, the affected-row count for UPDATE is the number of rows changed, not rows matched. An existing device row whose client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at already equal the supplied values can produce 0 affected rows and be rejected incorrectly. Use CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS, a follow-up existence check, or otherwise distinguish 'updated an existing row' from 'no matching row'.

findings.title: Authn client is coupled to the anonstore storage package for a sentinel error
findings.body: Authenticate imports pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore and uses errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached). This couples the authentication client to a concrete database-store implementation. The sentinel error should be part of the anonymous service contract or a shared service package so alternate anonymous.Service implementations can signal the same condition without importing storage internals.
